title: Cumulative assessment: Days 1–24
orientation: Attempt these newly authored items without the lesson open, then use their explanations and writing rubrics to plan targeted revision. Earlier phase concepts remain available for review. This is a self-study assessment; there is no time-to-expertise or examination-mark guarantee.

items.prompt: Choose the present-perfect passive: The clerk has signed the copies.
options: The copies have been signed by the clerk.
The copies has signed by the clerk.
The copies have being signed by the clerk.
The copies had sign by the clerk.
items.why: Have been signed preserves present-perfect structure and adds passive be + past participle with plural subject agreement.

items.prompt: Which is an established prepositional passive?
options: The issue was happened yesterday.
The issue was arrived at noon.
The issue was consisted four parts.
The issue was referred to in the report.
items.why: Refer to can license a passive whose subject corresponds to the preposition’s complement. Ordinary happen, arrive and consist do not license those proposed passive patterns.

items.prompt: I stopped to read the notice normally means:
options: The notice forced me to stop reading.
Reading the notice had already finished.
I ceased reading the notice.
I paused another activity in order to read the notice.
items.why: The infinitive states the purpose of stopping. Stopped reading would mean ending the reading activity.

items.prompt: Which sentence explicitly identifies the reader in its opening adjunct?
options: Having read the draft, the error was Maya.
Reading the draft, Maya’s error noticed the editor.
After Maya read the draft, the error became obvious.
After reading the draft, the error corrected Maya.
items.why: The finite after-clause supplies Maya as its subject, avoiding a dangling interpretation.

items.prompt: A fact still holds. Which report is possible in an appropriate present context?
options: She said that the office is open on Sundays.
She said that is the office open on Sundays.
She said that the office opening on Sundays.
She said that the office has open on Sundays.
items.why: Present tense can be retained when the reporter presents the information as currently true. Backshift is not a compulsory mechanical substitution in every report.

items.prompt: Report Did the manager approve it? after The clerk asked.
options: The clerk asked whether the manager had approved it.
The clerk asked that whether the manager had approved it.
The clerk asked whether had the manager approved it.
The clerk asked did the manager approve it.
items.why: Whether introduces the embedded yes/no interrogative; statement order and ordinary past-report backshift fit this context.

items.prompt: The analyst saw the guard with a telescope. Which judgement is justified without context?
options: Only the guard can have the telescope.
Only the analyst can use the telescope.
Attachment of with a telescope can be ambiguous.
The sentence lacks a finite verb.
items.why: The prepositional phrase can describe an instrument of seeing or modify the guard. Context or rephrasing can clarify attachment.

items.prompt: Which version explicitly compares rent with rent without relying on an unstated comparison?
options: Our rent is higher than the neighbouring office.
Our rent is higher than that of the neighbouring office.
Our rent is higher than the office is expensive.
Our rent is higher than neighbouring.
items.why: That of the neighbouring office compares rent with rent, rather than rent with a building or office.

items.prompt: Front negative never with appropriate inversion: We have never seen such flooding.
options: Never we have seen such flooding.
Never have we seen such flooding.
Never have seen we such flooding.
Never we seen have such flooding.
items.why: A fronted negative adverbial normally triggers subject–auxiliary inversion: have precedes we.

items.prompt: In Nina can attend, and so can Omar, so helps express:
options: a possessive relationship
substitution/reduced repetition of the predicate
an obligatory result clause
a negative condition
items.why: The second clause avoids repeating attend; positive additive so + inverted auxiliary links Omar’s ability to Nina’s.

items.prompt: Several teachers have separate schedules. Which plural possessive is standard?
options: the teacher’s schedules, necessarily meaning several teachers
the teachers schedules’
the teachers’ schedules
the teachers’s schedules
items.why: The regular plural teachers ends in s, so its possessive apostrophe follows s.

items.prompt: Which statement about quotation marks is accurate?
options: Nested quotations never need distinct marks.
Only double outer quotation marks are grammatical.
Only single outer quotation marks are grammatical.
Established styles use either single or double outer marks, with consistent nesting.
items.why: Quotation-mark conventions vary between publishers and regions. Consistency and clear nesting matter; one house style is not a universal grammar law.

items.prompt: Which plural belongs to the ordinary noun criterion?
options: criterias
criteriones
criteria
criterionses
items.why: Criteria is the established plural of criterion in ordinary formal usage; an extra plural ending is unnecessary.

items.prompt: Select the ordinary object form: The invitation was sent to my brother and ____.
options: me
my
mine
I
items.why: To takes the whole coordinated complement my brother and me. Coordination does not require subject case.

items.prompt: We have been reviewing the files since dawn. Which claim follows from the verb form alone?
options: An activity is viewed over a period connected to now; completion is not guaranteed.
The activity cannot have just stopped.
Every file has been reviewed.
The review occurred only last year.
items.why: Perfect progressive relates an extended activity to now; it does not guarantee completion and can describe recently stopped activity.

items.prompt: The price of the replacement parts ____ unexpectedly high.
options: be
is
are
have
items.why: Singular price controls agreement. Parts is inside the modifying of-phrase.

items.prompt: Choose a standard embedded question after Please tell me.
options: where is the next meeting
that where the next meeting is
where does the next meeting is
where the next meeting is
items.why: The embedded question has subject before finite verb: the next meeting is. Direct-question inversion is not used.

items.prompt: Which report preserves uncertainty in The lock may be damaged?
options: The lock is certainly damaged.
The lock might be damaged.
The lock must be replaced immediately.
The lock has definitely failed.
items.why: Might can preserve a tentative possibility. The other options add certainty, a requirement or a confirmed failure.

items.prompt: Make The archivist has catalogued the letters passive without changing the tense-aspect.
items.model: The letters have been catalogued by the archivist.
rubric: Use plural have and passive been catalogued.
alternatives: A different response is valid if it preserves the specified meaning and satisfies every stated structural constraint.

items.prompt: Offer two paraphrases of The reviewer discussed the report with the appendix, one for each plausible attachment.
items.model: The reviewer used the appendix while discussing the report. / The reviewer discussed the report that included the appendix.
rubric: Make the two intended attachments explicit.
State that context is needed to select the intended meaning.
alternatives: A different response is valid if it preserves the specified meaning and satisfies every stated structural constraint.

items.prompt: Write a 90–120-word meeting report. Include a passive, an attributed statement, an embedded question and a clear parallel list. Identify the structures after the passage.
items.model:
The revised catalogue was discussed at Monday’s staff meeting. The curator said that several descriptions still needed checking against the original records. She asked whether the volunteers had recorded uncertain dates separately. The coordinator explained that a special column had been added for that purpose. Staff agreed to check the names, compare the dates and record unresolved questions before the next review. Only after those checks have been completed will the catalogue be prepared for public use. The team will retain the earlier version so that later editors can trace each amendment. The report records the agreed procedure without claiming that every description is already accurate.

Analysis: was discussed is a passive. Said that attributes a claim. Whether the volunteers had recorded is an embedded question with subject–auxiliary order. Check, compare and record form a parallel list.
rubric: Write 90–120 words of connected prose, excluding the grammatical annotation.
Include every requested construction and identify its form and meaning.
Check reference, tense, clause boundaries and meaning; this is self-review, not an external grade.
alternatives: A different response is valid if it preserves the specified meaning and satisfies every stated structural constraint.
